name: Mulaha
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Kwalean language; only wordlist/classification material (Dutton 1975) found, no phonological description

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1975. South-eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (PL C-38), 613-664. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Nothing; no occurrence of stress/accent/tone in the chapter. §2.9.5.3 Kwalean (p. 636): Mulaha (or Iaibu) extinct, 'short vocabularies and some sentences of which were published by English (1901) and Ray (1907:387-412)'; 'Not much is known about the grammar of either Kwale or Humene except for the notes I published in Dutton 1970'.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1970. Notes on the languages of the Rigo area of the Central District of Papua. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific Linguistic Studies in honour of Arthur Capell (PL C-13), 879-983. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Silent on Mulaha. §2.23 (pp. 890-891) says the only record of Mulaha/Iaibu is English's 1900-1 vocabulary and Lawes's wordlist in Ray 1907:387-412; Appendix 3.7 'Some phonological aspects of Kwalean and Manubaran languages' (pp. 916-917) sketches Kwale and Humene only ('None of the languages is tonal but stress seems to be phonemic in each... Stress is phonemic, e.g. ma'ia sun and 'maia mountain' for Kwale) and does not cover Mulaha.

sources.citation: Ray, S. H. 1907. Papuan languages of Central British New Guinea, §16 Mulaha and Iaibu. In Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol. III: Linguistics, 352-354 (vocabulary no. 35 pp. 387-412). Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
sources.note: Silent. '1. Phonology. Vowels: a, e, i, o, u. Consonants: k, g; t, d; p, b, v; r; m, n; s, h. In (I.) w is used for v and u...' — inventory only, compiled from Lawes's 1898 elicitation from the last speaker; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mula1254 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Nothing; cites only Dutton 1975:636 (subclassification) and Moseley 2010 (extinct). Glottolog descriptive refs for mfw: Dutton 1994 (overview), Ray 1929 (overview), English 1902 (wordlist) — no grammar/phonology entry.

sources.citation: Ray, S. H. 1929. The languages of the Central Division of Papua. JRAI 59: 65-96.
